native_result.query: What types of plant introductions were influenced by urban land use?
native_result.HypoA: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.
native_result.HypoB: Urban land use has influenced two types of plant introductions at different stages of the invasion process: (1) unintentional introductions (contaminated seed lots, trade, tourism) are the pathway most strongly influenced by urban land use at the local establishment scale — their records are over-represented in urbanized plots (36% of records in 'Urban' habitat vs 28.3% baseline, enrichment 1.27; Gardening-vs-Unintentional chi2=3.84, p=0.05), their share within occupied plots increases with urban cover in the surrounding 500–1000 m landscape (+0.74 log-odds per unit urban.2009.500m, 95% CI [-0.27, +1.74], LRT p=0.14, consistent at 500 m and 1000 m in 2009 but absent at 50 m and for 1956 cover, implying contemporary landscape-scale urbanization rather than the plot itself), and these species form a phylogenetically clustered urban/ruderal assemblage (within-pathway patristic distance 183 vs null 208, p=0.001) with the widest habitat ranges (2.72) and most invaded plots (mean 9.5). (2) Gardening/ornamental introductions were influenced by urban land use at the introduction-effort scale over time, not at local establishment: Catalonia-wide their share of new introductions rose from 16.8% (before 1500) to 75.2% (1985–2019, the period of modern urban growth), yet established gardening species are not concentrated near urban cover (urban.2009.500m coefficient -0.80, CI [-1.82, +0.22], p=0.11; Urban-habitat enrichment 0.94) because ornamentals persist across many habitats (44% trees/shrubs). (3) Agriculture/forestry introductions show no urban influence (coefficient +0.09, CI [-2.54, +2.72], p=1.00) and are urban-avoiding (only 8.7% of records in Urban habitat, enrichment 0.31). In short, urban land use promoted accidental/unintentional introductions where aliens establish, drove the temporal explosion of ornamental (gardening) introductions, and left agriculture/forestry introductions unaffected.

Models: (a) presence of aliens on all 632 plots; (b) pathway composition (n.gard/n.unint/n.agfo out of n.total) on the 191 occupied plots with primary exposure urban.2009.500m controlling for elevation, habitat (10 levels), annual temperature/rainfall, log distance to road/stream; (c) sensitivity with urban.1956.500m, urban.2009.50m, urban.2009.1000m; (d) secondary models adding progressive landscape-change fractions; (e) residual Moran's I diagnostics (k=8 nearest neighbours, 199 permutations); (f) descriptive urban-habitat enrichment with chi2; (g) Catalonia-wide temporal pathway shares as separate descriptive corroboration; (h) species-level summaries on 77 unique species (4 duplicates dropped); (i) optional phylogenetic robustness via 999-permutation test of within-pathway mean patristic distance using a hand-parsed Newick tree.
